GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.

GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map molecular assemblies across the Golgi interactome. The work aims to define complexes beyond the well-characterized subset, potentially revealing unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms underlying Golgi trafficking and homeostasis.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-Oct-29 Medium

Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.

This study takes a family-level approach to structural clustering across the tree of life, analyzing 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database to identify candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs. The authors find a shared expansion of solenoid protein families, suggesting these structural motifs played a role in the transition from prokaryotes to eukaryotes. This family-level structural profiling complements sequence-based homology detection, which is limited by deep evolutionary divergence.

Development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors for metabolic diseases.

The authors report the development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors, targeting a liver-exclusive enzyme that controls production of 12α-hydroxylated bile acids. Inhibiting this enzyme is proposed as a therapeutic strategy to remodel bile acid balance and the gut microbiota for treating metabolic diseases, addressing a gap caused by the structural similarity of CYP8B1's active site to other cytochrome P450 enzymes.

Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.

The authors used computational docking (HDOCK) and AlphaFold3 modeling to screen 34 swine deubiquitinating enzymes for interaction with the ASFV ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L, identifying FAM105A as the top candidate. Co-immunoprecipitation experimentally confirmed the I215L–FAM105A interaction, and structural analyses characterized the binding interface. This provides a candidate host factor for ASFV replication that could inform antiviral strategies.

HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.

The authors present HelixWings, an AI-driven screening platform that combines conformational dynamics analysis with sequence-based prediction to engineer enzymes that can use cheaper biomimetic cofactors like NMNH instead of natural NADPH. This addresses the poor activity natural enzymes typically show toward alternative cofactors, offering a computational alternative to slow directed evolution and complex rational design. The work demonstrates a practical route to lowering synthesis costs in cofactor-dependent biocatalysis.

AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.

The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of the syphilis pathogen Treponema pallidum Nichols strain. This approach assigned structural and functional clues to previously uncharacterized proteins, including roughly 17% of the 977 annotated proteins that lack sequence-based functional annotation, offering a clearer view of the organism's biology and pathogenic traits.

Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network.

This study investigates how two structurally similar pigment-protein subunits of photosystem II—the minor antenna complex CP29 and the major complex LHCII—achieve distinct functional roles in light harvesting. Using 2D electronic-vibrational spectroscopy combined with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling, the authors assign spectral features to specific exciton states and show that subtle structural differences tune energy transfer specialization. The work provides molecular-level insight into how subunit diversity shapes the PSII antenna network's function.

By systematically sampling PFAS head group types, the approach aims to rationalize how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic wettability, supporting the search for sustainable alternatives to persistent PFAS chemistries.

Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.

This review surveys molecular dynamics simulation methods for studying graphene and graphene-derived ionic liquid supercapacitors, focusing on how electrode-charging schemes (fixed/constant charge, constant potential, electronic-structure-aware approaches) capture interfacial structure and capacitance. It argues that molecular-scale simulations are essential because continuum theory and experiment alone cannot resolve the relevant length and time scales. The paper serves as a methodological guide for computational electrochemistry of graphene-based energy storage interfaces.

Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.

This paper revisits a theoretical prediction that strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities can invert the intrinsic regioselectivity of electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene, acting like a "photonic substituent." Using correlated ab initio cavity QED methods (QED-DFT geometry relaxations plus QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations on Wheland intermediates), the authors confirm substantial energetic reordering of the reaction pathways. The work supports the idea that cavity vacuum fields can exert electronic and structural control over ground-state chemical reactivity.

The information content of ultrafast observables: spectroscopy and scattering in excited norbornadiene.

This study evaluates how well different time-resolved spectroscopy and scattering techniques can distinguish between competing computational models of an ultrafast photochemical reaction. Using norbornadiene photoisomerisation as a test case, the authors simulate dynamics at four levels of electronic structure theory and compute the resulting photoelectron spectra and electron/X-ray scattering signals. They find that these observables have varying sensitivity to the underlying nonadiabatic dynamics, providing guidance on which experimental probes are most informative for characterising ultrafast reactions.

Uncertainty Quantification for Free Energy Calculations by Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Inference.

This paper introduces a generalized hierarchical Bayesian inference framework for quantifying uncertainty in free energy calculations, addressing the limitations of existing Gaussian process implementations that typically condition on limited data. The method aims to better distinguish genuine physical features in free energy profiles from artifacts caused by insufficient sampling or simulation noise. It provides a more principled way to assess confidence in free energy predictions from molecular dynamics simulations.

MARS: Machine-Learned Force Field Framework for Automated Conformational Sampling, Vibrational Spectroscopy, and Microsolvation.

MARS is an open-source Python package that automates conformational sampling, infrared spectrum prediction, and explicit microsolvation using machine-learned force fields (SO3LR and MACE) with GPU acceleration via JAX. It combines metadynamics, multitemperature molecular dynamics, and genetic algorithms in a four-phase workflow, and includes automated vibrational mode classification via Wilson B-matrix projections. The tool lowers the barrier to MLFF-based spectroscopy and solvation studies for non-specialists.

EZpred: Improving Deep Learning-Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs.

Orf virus early genes ORFV113 and ORFV114 are individually dispensable for replication in vitro but required for full virulence in vivo.

This study shows that the Orf virus genes ORFV113 and ORFV114, located in the variable terminal region of the genome, are not needed for the virus to replicate in cultured lamb testis cells, since single-gene deletion mutants grew normally in vitro. However, deleting either gene reduced the virus's ability to cause disease in vivo, indicating both contribute to full virulence. The work characterizes their transcription and uses homologous recombination to build reporter-tagged deletion mutants.

Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Cofolding Models: Correct Ligand Placement Is Decoupled From Accurate Protein Conformation.

This benchmark evaluates four leading AI cofolding models (AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1) on kinase and Class A GPCR complexes and finds that correctly placing the ligand does not imply the surrounding protein conformation is accurately predicted. In other words, a model can dock a ligand plausibly into a mispredicted fold, so ligand-placement metrics alone can overstate structural accuracy. The work highlights the need to assess protein conformation and ligand placement separately when using cofolding models.
